signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.79, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.96, 160.48, and 158.45. A 275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate spread and +268bp OIS carry differential favor USD, yet JPY leveraged funds net short sits at an extreme -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18) after a heavy WoW liquidation of -29,678 contracts. Saxo 25-delta risk reversals trade at -2.54, reflecting deep put skew and substantial downside protection demand. Emerging Strait of Hormuz maritime security tensions introduce headline vulnerability to crowded short positions while VIX remains contained at 14.5. The combination of stretched short positioning and heavy downside hedging leaves USD/JPY vulnerable to rapid short covering if Middle East disruption accelerates. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside squeeze risk against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Fed reiterates hawkish stance while Strait of Hormuz disruptions resolve, renewing carry-driven upside.

signals.title: AUD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers an active bilateral theme, with leader AUD averaging +0.335% across 4 pairs and laggard SEK averaging -0.601% across 2 pairs, producing a 0.935% spread that exceeds the 0.80% threshold. RBA policy rate at 4.35% (on hold) stands against Riksbank at 1.75% (on hold), establishing a 260bp nominal rate advantage for the Australian Dollar. Sweden CPIF printed soft this morning at 0.7% YoY versus 0.8% forecast alongside -0.3% MoM, cementing SEK weakness across European desks. Australia's positive ESI of +16.3 directly opposes Sweden's negative reading of -26.7, confirming diverging economic momentum. Macro and policy fundamentals continue to align behind cross-currency divergence. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/SEK, supported by carry advantage and diverging macroeconomic momentum. Catalyst: Riksbank meeting 24 Sep. Risk: G10 scorecard spread compresses below 0.80% as Scandinavian data stabilizes.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7219, advancing above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7135, 0.7041, and 0.6988. Leveraged funds hold net long +50,250 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.79), placing institutional positioning in the top decile of its 52-week range despite a WoW trimming of -3,328 contracts. Meanwhile, Myfxbook retail sentiment registers an extreme 90% short bias, creating direct divergence against speculative positioning. The RBA at 4.35% versus the Fed at 3.75% delivers a 60bp nominal carry advantage (69bp OIS carry in favor of AUD). Contrarian retail positioning and constructive carry support upward momentum, but extended institutional length signals late-cycle trend expansion. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; crowded institutional long positioning tempers extension velocity. Catalyst: Fed meeting 16 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds accelerate weekly profit taking below 0.7135, triggering broader long unwinds.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium + Technical Resistance
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3527, holding below its SMA20 at 1.3555 while remaining above the SMA50 at 1.3456 and SMA200 at 1.3447. CBOE 1-month implied volatility sits at 11.0% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, generating an elevated volatility risk premium of +6.3%. Fed policy rate at 3.75% versus BoE at 3.75% yields 0bp nominal spread, with SONIA versus SOFR pricing a tight -7bp carry differential. Leveraged funds maintain net long +47,504 contracts (pctl 93, z +1.27) following a weekly reduction of -9,335 contracts. High options premium reflects significant event-risk hedging into US inflation data and UK parliamentary hearings. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; heavy volatility hedging restricts directional breakout follow-through. Catalyst: BoE Monetary Policy Report Hearings today at 13:15 UTC. Risk: A daily close above 1.3555 dismantles local technical resistance and compresses the vol premium.
